attractions.name: Tomb of Bulleh Shah
attractions.description: The shrine of Bulleh Shah, one of the most celebrated Punjabi Sufi poets, a significant pilgrimage and cultural site.

attractions.name: Kasur old city bazaars
attractions.description: Historic markets known for traditional shoes (khussa), textiles, and local crafts.

transportation.notes: Rickshaws are common for short trips

accommodations.name: Mid-range hotel near the main bazaar

weather_info.climate_type: Semi-arid, continental climate with hot summers and cool winters

travel_tips.tip: Kasur is a short, easy day trip from Lahore, well connected by a direct road.
Rickshaws are the easiest way to get around the compact old city area.
Standard travel precautions apply in busy bazaar areas.
Visit the shrine of Bulleh Shah in the evening, when it's most atmospheric and often features devotional music.

history.founded: An old city with a history stretching back several centuries
history.city_history: Kasur is best known as the home and burial place of Bulleh Shah, one of the most revered Sufi poets in the Punjabi language, whose verses remain widely sung and quoted across Punjab today. The city has long been known for its traditional leather shoe (khussa) making craft.
history.province_history: Punjab, meaning 'land of five rivers', has one of the longest continuous histories in South Asia, home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa), later ruled by the Mauryas, Mughals, Sikh Empire, and the British before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947.
